title: Introspective build profiler and fast-patch rebuild flow for CI
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem: cold rebuilds for incremental developer changes are still a major time sink. We see repeated full-step cache misses across everyday edits (tests, linters, small backend fixes). Goal: cut developer iteration latency by 3x for small patches and reduce CI resource waste by improving cache hit rates across steps.

What we'll build: 1) a lightweight 'introspective profiler' that runs as a short pre-step in CI to compute file- and module-level change fingerprints for the current patch; 2) a fast-patch rebuild flow that uses the profiler to prune the build graph and only run affected build steps and test subsets; 3) step-level cache keys and TTLs (per-tool, e.g., linter, deps, transpile) so we don't invalidate unrelated caches; 4) an agent prewarm hook to opportunistically prime hot caches on ephemeral CI runners; and 5) observability: per-run metrics (cache-hits, skipped-steps, end-to-end time) surfaced in Console and used to auto-tune TTLs and prewarm heuristics.

Design decisions: - Use a compiled Rust binary for fingerprinting for performance and low overhead on runners; provide small Node shim for local dev. - Cache-key format: sha256(file-fingerprint||step-id||tool-version) with optional short name for readability. - Fall back to full build if profiler fails (fail-open). - Rollout via canary on low-risk repos, then platform teams.

Compatibility & integration: integrates with remote CAS and existing buildkit-based builders. Will add GraphQL flag to existing CI orchestration API to request 'fast-patch' mode.

Success criteria: - 3x median reduction in restart-to-green time for PRs with <=10 changed files; - 20% overall CI GPU/CPU runtime reduction in the first 90 days; - increased cache hit rate for lint/compile steps by 30%.
comments: 2026-01-27 — Kickoff: scoping done with Platform and DX. Agreed success metrics and canary plan. Action: Jun to prototype profiler CLI (P0).

2026-02-02 — Prototype ready: Rust binary can fingerprint repo in ~120ms for small services. Initial synthetic tests show ~45% skipped steps on a 6-file change. PR: github.com/redwood/ci/compare/PR-4856

2026-02-11 — Design review with Security. Security asked for deterministic hashing and reproducible behavior across architectures. Decided: include explicit sorting and normalization step in fingerprinting. Security review required: false (per policy) but follow deterministic guidance.

2026-02-18 — Experiment on plumbing-service: added step-level TTL of 7d for linter cache and 24h for transpile cache. Observed 28% runtime reduction on patch runs, minor cache churn on master. Logged observations in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/BUILD/fast-patch-experiments

2026-02-24 — Blocker found: some legacy build steps depend on WORKDIR side effects; added safe-detection heuristics and a conservative fallback to full build when ambiguous. Follow-up: tech debt ticket ENG-331919 to remediate side-effectful steps.
2026-03-01 — UX: added CLI flag --simulate to show which steps would run without executing. Request from DX: surface simulate output in PR checks. Pending UI task for Console team.
2026-03-04 — Canary rollout plan approved. Stage 1: 10 repos (low-risk infra + libraries) for 2 weeks. Stage 2: cross-org ramp with metrics gating. Release target: ci-runtime-2026.03-alpha
notes: Trade-offs: choosing Rust improves fingerprint speed but increases cross-compile maintenance. We mitigate by shipping prebuilt binaries for common CI platforms and a Node fallback for local developers. Observability hooks will drive tuning; initial TTLs are conservative to avoid cache thrash. Follow-ups: document patterns for writing side-effect-free steps and add builder liveness telemetry to detect failed prewarm attempts.
